library_guide_intro: Learn one rule at a time. Open an example and walk through what happens.
library_uno_summary: Empty your hand before anyone else. Each turn, match the color, number, or symbol on the discard pile, or use a Wild to choose a new color. Skips and Reverses change who plays next, while draw cards can build a penalty that another player must take. Keep an eye on every shrinking hand: you need to declare UNO before leaving yourself with one card, and you can catch someone who forgets. This app uses its own clearly explained stacking and drawing rules. It is a lively game of quick decisions, changing fortunes, and watching your friends very closely.
library_catan_summary: Build a small settlement into a thriving network of roads and cities. Dice determine which landscapes produce resources, so every placement shapes what you can afford later. Trade with the bank or negotiate with friends to get the materials you need. Expand toward useful land and harbors, upgrade settlements, and use development cards to create new opportunities. Roads and knights can earn special awards, but a robber can interrupt a productive region. The first active player to reach ten points wins. Choose a beginner island to get going quickly, or place your starting settlements yourself in the variable setup.
library_carcassonne_summary: Build a countryside together, one tile at a time. Extend roads, enclose cities, and surround monasteries while deciding where your limited meeples will earn the most points. A figure claims a connected feature, but separate regions can merge later and change who receives the score. Completed features return most pieces to your supply; farmers usually stay until the end. Every new tile can finish your work or complicate somebody else’s plans. Start with the learning setup, or add optional Big Box 3.1 expansions for special figures and new decisions. The shared host setup lets your group choose how much to include.
learn_uno_deal_info: Deal seven cards to each player. Start with a number card; the first seat plays clockwise.
learn_uno_deal_before: Ada, Bea and Leo sit in that order.
learn_uno_deal_action: Deal seven each and reveal a red 7.
learn_uno_deal_result: Ada plays first. The next ordinary turn is Bea’s.
learn_uno_match_info: Match the active color, number or action symbol. Wild cards are another option.
learn_uno_match_before: The discard is a red 7. Ada has red 3, blue 7 and blue 5.
learn_uno_match_action: Compare each card with the red 7.
learn_uno_match_result: Red 3 and blue 7 work. Blue 5 matches neither color nor number.
learn_uno_draw_info: You may draw even with a playable card. In these house rules, drawing one immediately ends your turn.
learn_uno_draw_before: Ada could play red 3 on red 7, but chooses to draw.
learn_uno_draw_result: The card stays in her hand. Bea plays next; Ada cannot play the drawn card now.
learn_uno_skip_info: Skip passes over the next seat in the current direction.
learn_uno_skip_before: The order is Ada → Bea → Leo.
learn_uno_reverse_info: Reverse flips the direction. With two players it acts like Skip.
learn_uno_reverse_before: In a three-player game, Bea would follow Ada.
learn_uno_reverse_result: Leo plays next. With only Ada and Bea, Ada plays again instead.
learn_uno_wild_info: A Wild changes the active color. The color choice must finish before any ordinary action continues.
learn_uno_wild_before: Ada has a Wild (✦) and wants blue next.
learn_uno_wild_action: She plays it and chooses blue.
learn_uno_wild_result: Bea must match blue or play another legal Wild. The Wild has no fixed printed color.
learn_uno_pay_info: Drawing the penalty clears the stack and loses your turn. Ordinary cards cannot answer a penalty.
learn_uno_pay_before: Leo faces six cards and has no legal stack.
learn_uno_pay_result: The penalty becomes zero and Ada takes the next turn.
learn_uno_declare_info: With two cards, arm UNO before playing one. The declaration and play are submitted together.
learn_uno_declare_action: Ada activates UNO and plays one card.
learn_uno_declare_result: She has one declared card and cannot be caught for this play.
learn_uno_catch_info: Any opponent may catch an undeclared one-card hand for a two-card penalty. Catching does not use the opponent’s turn.
learn_uno_catch_before: Ada plays from two cards to one without declaring.
learn_uno_catch_action: Bea catches her before the next accepted play or draw.
learn_uno_catch_result: Ada draws two, leaving three. Bea still has her ordinary turn. Only one catch succeeds.
learn_uno_win_info: An empty hand wins. A final Wild still needs its color choice. A final-card win cancels outstanding penalties and catches; there is no round scoring.
learn_uno_win_action: Ada plays it and chooses green.
learn_uno_win_result: Ada wins. Bea does not draw four, and no further stacking is allowed.
learn_uno_reshuffle_info: When the stock is empty, keep the top discard and shuffle the earlier discards into a new stock.
learn_uno_reshuffle_before: The stock is empty. Red 7 is on top of several discards.
learn_uno_reshuffle_action: Shuffle only the cards underneath red 7.
learn_uno_reshuffle_result: Red 7 remains the matching target; the recycled cards can be drawn.
learn_catan_setup_info: The beginner setup places starting pieces for you. Variable setup uses forward then reverse seat order, placing one settlement and adjacent road each time.
learn_catan_setup_before: Ada, Bea and Leo choose variable setup.
learn_catan_setup_action: They place in order Ada, Bea, Leo, then Leo, Bea, Ada.
learn_catan_setup_result: Each has two settlements and two roads. Resources come from the land touching their second settlement.
learn_catan_production_info: A matching number produces one resource per adjacent settlement or two per city. Everyone can collect, not only the roller.
learn_catan_production_before: Ada’s settlement and Bea’s city touch a forest numbered 6.
learn_catan_production_result: Ada receives one lumber and Bea receives two, provided the bank has enough. A robber on this hex would block both.
learn_catan_shortage_info: For a resource shortage affecting several recipients, nobody receives that resource. A sole recipient receives the remaining stock.
learn_catan_shortage_before: Ada and Bea each need two grain; the bank has three.
learn_catan_shortage_action: Demand is four, above the bank’s three.
learn_catan_shortage_result: Both receive zero grain. If Ada alone needed four, she would receive all three remaining grain.
learn_catan_distance_info: A settlement cannot occupy an intersection beside any building, including your own. A city can only upgrade your own settlement.
learn_catan_distance_before: Ada wants to build immediately beside Bea’s settlement.
learn_catan_distance_action: Compare the neighboring point with a free point two edges away.
learn_catan_distance_result: The neighbor is illegal. The farther point can work if it connects to Ada’s road and has no other neighboring building.
learn_catan_supplies_info: Each player has 15 roads, 5 settlements and 4 cities. You need a spare piece to build it.
learn_catan_supplies_before: Ada has all five settlement pieces on the island.
learn_catan_supplies_action: She upgrades one to a city.
learn_catan_supplies_result: One settlement returns to supply and can be built elsewhere later. Cities do not create extra settlement pieces.
learn_catan_bank_info: Trade four of one resource for one different resource. An owned generic harbor improves this to 3:1; a matching resource harbor gives 2:1.
learn_catan_bank_before: Ada needs ore and owns a lumber harbor.
learn_catan_bank_action: She gives two lumber for one ore.
learn_catan_bank_result: The trade works if ore remains in the bank. Her lumber harbor does not improve exchanges of grain.
learn_catan_offers_info: Player trades involve the active player. When a rival accepts the active player’s offer, the active player confirms the partner before resources move.
learn_catan_offers_before: Ada offers one lumber for Bea’s brick.
learn_catan_offers_action: Bea accepts; Ada confirms Bea as the partner.
learn_catan_offers_result: One resource goes each way. An acceptance alone did not move them. Either decline or withdrawal can end an unfinished offer.
learn_catan_seven_title: Discard half if you hold more than seven
learn_catan_seven_info: On seven, every player with more than seven resource cards discards half, rounded down. Development cards do not count.
learn_catan_seven_before: Ada has nine resources and two development cards.
learn_catan_seven_action: Bea rolls seven; Ada chooses four resources to discard.
learn_catan_seven_result: Ada keeps five resources and both development cards. Nobody receives production from a seven.
learn_catan_robber_info: After discards, the roller moves the robber to another hex and chooses an adjacent opponent. One resource is stolen randomly if that opponent has any.
learn_catan_robber_before: Bea moves the robber to Ada’s productive forest.
learn_catan_robber_action: Bea selects Ada as the victim.
learn_catan_robber_result: Bea takes one random resource, not a resource she chooses. That forest produces nothing while blocked.
learn_catan_timing_info: You may play at most one action development card per opportunity, and cannot play a card bought in that same opportunity. Victory points are private passive points.
learn_catan_timing_before: Ada buys a Knight during her actions.
learn_catan_timing_action: She tries to use it immediately.
learn_catan_timing_result: It must wait for a later opportunity. An older eligible action card can be played, even before rolling.
learn_catan_knight_info: Play a Knight to move the robber and steal. Played Knights count toward Largest Army.
learn_catan_knight_before: Ada has an older Knight and the robber blocks her field.
learn_catan_knight_action: She plays the Knight and moves the robber away.
learn_catan_knight_result: She can steal from a chosen adjacent rival; this also adds one to her played Knights.
learn_catan_monopoly_info: Choose one resource type. All opponents give you all their cards of that type.
learn_catan_monopoly_before: Bea has two wool and Leo has three wool.
learn_catan_monopoly_action: Ada plays Monopoly and chooses wool.
learn_catan_monopoly_result: Ada receives five wool. Other resource types and the bank remain untouched.
learn_catan_invention_info: Choose two resources from available bank stock. They may be the same type if the bank has two.
learn_catan_invention_before: Ada needs two ore and the bank has two.
learn_catan_invention_action: She plays Invention and chooses both ore.
learn_catan_invention_result: Two ore move to Ada. A choice exceeding bank stock is unavailable.
learn_catan_longest_info: A qualifying route has at least five roads and gives two points. Opposing buildings interrupt it. Count a continuous trail without reusing an edge.
learn_catan_longest_before: Ada holds the award with five roads; Bea reaches five too.
learn_catan_longest_action: Bea adds a sixth road to her continuous route.
learn_catan_longest_result: The tie alone kept Ada’s award; six takes it for Bea. A branch is not automatically part of one trail.
learn_catan_army_info: At least three played Knights qualify for two points. The holder keeps a tie; a strictly larger army takes it.
learn_catan_army_before: Ada has played three Knights and owns Largest Army.
learn_catan_army_action: Bea goes from three to four played Knights.
learn_catan_army_result: Bea takes the award. Unplayed Knight cards do not count.
learn_catan_victory_info: The active player wins at ten total points, including private victory-point cards. Settlements give one, cities two, and each award two.
learn_catan_victory_before: Ada has eight public points and two private victory-point cards.
learn_catan_victory_action: Her active opportunity reaches the victory check.
learn_catan_victory_result: Her ten total points win; hidden victory points become visible with the winner announcement.
learn_catan_paired_info: After the primary player, the player three seats ahead receives an action opportunity. They do not roll or trade with players, but may build, trade with the bank and use eligible development cards.
learn_catan_paired_before: Six seats are Ada, Bea, Leo, Dani, Eva and Fran.
learn_catan_paired_action: Ada rolls and finishes her actions. Dani takes the paired opportunity.
learn_catan_paired_result: Dani acts without rolling. After Dani ends, Bea becomes the next primary player and rolls.
learn_carcassonne_setup_info: The room host chooses the preset, optional modules and starting player. Everyone reviews the same configuration; changes clear readiness.
learn_carcassonne_setup_before: Ada hosts; Bea is a guest.
learn_carcassonne_setup_action: Ada chooses Learn and both confirm readiness.
learn_carcassonne_setup_result: The shared game begins. Solo practice instead confirms all local seats from one Start practice button.
learn_carcassonne_turn_info: Draw and place a tile, optionally deploy a figure, then resolve scoring and any expansion choices. Expansion effects may add decisions around these steps.
learn_carcassonne_turn_action: She places it legally and puts a meeple on its unoccupied road.
learn_carcassonne_turn_result: Any completed features score. If none finish, her meeple stays until that road scores later.
learn_carcassonne_matching_info: Road meets road, city meets city, field meets field. A tile must share an edge, not just a corner, with the landscape.
learn_carcassonne_matching_before: Ada’s tile has a road facing an existing city edge.
learn_carcassonne_matching_action: She rotates the preview to match the city and checks every other touching edge.
learn_carcassonne_matching_result: Only a rotation matching every neighbor can be confirmed. Diagonal contact alone cannot anchor a tile.
learn_carcassonne_unplaceable_title: Keep a tile if it fits anywhere
learn_carcassonne_unplaceable_info: The app checks every frontier space and all four rotations before discarding an unplaceable tile. An inconvenient legal tile cannot be rejected.
learn_carcassonne_unplaceable_before: Ada dislikes the first suggested location.
learn_carcassonne_unplaceable_action: Another edge of the landscape accepts the tile after rotation.
learn_carcassonne_unplaceable_result: Ada must choose a legal placement. Only no legal placements at all allows an automatic discard.
learn_carcassonne_deploy_info: An ordinary meeple deploys onto an unoccupied connected feature of the tile just placed. One occupied part makes the whole connected feature unavailable.
learn_carcassonne_deploy_before: Bea already has a meeple on a city several tiles away.
learn_carcassonne_deploy_action: Ada extends that same city with her new tile.
learn_carcassonne_deploy_result: Ada cannot place an ordinary meeple into that city. She may use a separate unoccupied feature on the new tile or skip deployment.
learn_carcassonne_merge_info: Players may claim separate features that later join. Scoring goes to the greatest meeple strength; every tied leader receives the full score.
learn_carcassonne_merge_before: Ada and Bea each own a separate city with one normal meeple.
learn_carcassonne_merge_action: A new tile joins and completes a city worth eight points.
learn_carcassonne_merge_result: Ada and Bea each score eight, not four. If Ada had strength two against Bea’s one, only Ada would score.
learn_carcassonne_road_info: A completed ordinary road scores one per distinct tile. Its scoring meeples return to supply.
learn_carcassonne_road_before: Ada’s road crosses three tiles with one end still open.
learn_carcassonne_road_action: A legal placement completes that three-tile road.
learn_carcassonne_road_result: Ada scores three and retrieves her meeple for later turns.
learn_carcassonne_city_info: An ordinary completed city scores two per distinct tile and two per shield. A closed wall completes the city.
learn_carcassonne_city_before: Ada’s city has three tiles and one shield.
learn_carcassonne_city_result: Ada receives 2 × (3 + 1) = 8 points. The meeple returns.
learn_carcassonne_monastery_info: A monastery is complete when all eight surrounding squares contain tiles. It scores its own tile plus those eight.
learn_carcassonne_monastery_before: Ada’s monastery has seven neighboring tiles.
learn_carcassonne_monastery_action: The eighth neighboring square is filled.
learn_carcassonne_monastery_result: Ada scores nine and returns her meeple. Corner neighbors count here, unlike tile-placement contact.
learn_carcassonne_farmers_info: A normal meeple placed lying down in a field becomes a farmer. Fields score three per distinct neighboring completed city at the end, for the majority owners.
learn_carcassonne_farmers_before: Ada’s field touches two completed cities; it touches one of them twice.
learn_carcassonne_farmers_action: Final scoring counts distinct completed cities, not contacts.
learn_carcassonne_farmers_result: Ada scores six if she has the majority. Farmers usually stay until game end and cannot also occupy roads or cities.
learn_carcassonne_final_info: At game end, roads score one per tile; cities one per tile and shield; monasteries/gardens count their tile and existing neighbors. Fields count completed cities only.
learn_carcassonne_final_before: Ada has an unfinished three-tile road, a three-tile city with one shield and a monastery with four neighbors.
learn_carcassonne_final_action: No more tiles remain, so final scoring starts.
learn_carcassonne_final_result: Those features score 3, 4 and 5. Completed-city examples use a different city multiplier.
learn_carcassonne_standard_info: A standing meeple has strength one on a road, city or monastery; lying down makes it a strength-one farmer. Standard supply starts at seven.
learn_carcassonne_standard_before: Ada has seven standard meeples available.
learn_carcassonne_standard_action: She deploys one on a road.
learn_carcassonne_standard_result: Six remain. The road meeple returns when scored; a farmer normally waits for final scoring. Figures cannot be freely moved between features.
learn_carcassonne_large_info: Inns & Cathedrals adds one large meeple. It deploys like a normal meeple but counts as two for majority, including as a farmer.
learn_carcassonne_large_before: Ada’s large meeple and Bea’s normal meeple end up in a joined city.
learn_carcassonne_large_action: The city completes for eight points.
learn_carcassonne_large_result: Ada wins strength 2 to 1 and scores eight. Strength changes ownership, not the feature’s point value. Both pieces return.
learn_carcassonne_river_info: Start at the source, extend the river, and finish with the lake before ordinary landscape draws. River edges must connect, with no prohibited immediate reversal or U-turn.
learn_carcassonne_river_before: A river bend is already in place.
learn_carcassonne_river_action: Ada previews the next bend and rotates it to continue legally.
learn_carcassonne_river_result: The river stays connected without turning straight back on itself. After the lake, ordinary landscape play continues; the water itself is not a scoring feature.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_info: The abbot has strength one and can occupy a monastery or garden. Instead of deploying a figure, you may recall your abbot for its current value.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_before: Ada’s abbot sits in a garden with four neighboring tiles.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_action: On her deployment step, Ada recalls it.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_result: Ada scores five and gets the abbot back. A fully surrounded garden/monastery scores nine and returns it normally.
learn_carcassonne_inn_info: A completed inn road scores two per tile. In Big Box 3.1 an unfinished inn road retains ordinary final points, rather than zero.
learn_carcassonne_inn_before: Ada’s three-tile inn road is one connection from completion.
learn_carcassonne_inn_result: Ada scores six. If it stayed unfinished until game end, it would score three in this version.
learn_carcassonne_cathedral_info: A completed cathedral city scores three per tile and shield. An unfinished one retains the ordinary final multiplier of one in this version.
learn_carcassonne_cathedral_before: Ada’s city has three tiles, one shield and a cathedral.
learn_carcassonne_cathedral_result: It scores 3 × (3 + 1) = 12. Unfinished at the end, the same city scores four, not zero.
learn_carcassonne_goods_info: The player completing a city collects its wine, grain and cloth symbols regardless of city ownership. Final majorities award ten per collected goods category, including ties.
learn_carcassonne_goods_before: Bea owns a city containing two cloth symbols.
learn_carcassonne_goods_action: Ada completes it using her tile.
learn_carcassonne_goods_result: Bea receives city points; Ada receives two cloth. A category with no collected tokens awards nobody ten points.
learn_carcassonne_builder_info: Your builder grants an extra turn when your new tile extends its feature, then returns. Ferry movement alone is not an extension for this purpose.
learn_carcassonne_builder_before: Ada’s builder is on a city with her meeple.
learn_carcassonne_builder_action: Ada adds a city tile to that feature.
learn_carcassonne_builder_result: Resolve all current choices, retrieve the builder and draw for the queued extra turn if a tile remains.
learn_carcassonne_pig_info: Completing a shield-bearing city triggers pigs. Each scores three per completed city neighboring its field, without majority, then returns and can bring its attached farmer home.
learn_carcassonne_pig_before: Ada has a pig in a field with two completed neighboring cities.
learn_carcassonne_pig_action: A shield-city completion triggers the pig choice.
learn_carcassonne_pig_result: Ada scores six and chooses whether her farmer returns too. The pig has no final field multiplier.
learn_carcassonne_flight_info: The server fixes the flight die before landing selection. Flying may join occupied incomplete roads, cities or monasteries; a miss has no fallback deployment.
learn_carcassonne_flight_before: Ada chooses flight instead of ordinary deployment.
learn_carcassonne_flight_action: The die sends her two tiles in the machine’s direction.
learn_carcassonne_flight_result: She chooses a legal landing feature there. If there is none, the flight fails and she cannot deploy elsewhere this turn.
learn_carcassonne_ferry_info: A ferry connects selected road arms. Placing or moving it recomputes road connections, allowing splits and new completions.
learn_carcassonne_ferry_before: A ferry joins Ada’s road to a longer open road.
learn_carcassonne_ferry_action: An allowed ferry move selects different arms.
learn_carcassonne_ferry_result: The old connection separates. Inspect the new components for completion and ownership; ferry movement alone never triggers a builder.
learn_carcassonne_gold_info: A gold tile places one ingot on itself and another on a chosen adjacent occupied tile. Completing a feature awards gold on its tiles to qualifying owners.
learn_carcassonne_gold_before: A completed shared feature includes three gold ingots. Ada and Bea tie.
learn_carcassonne_gold_action: Collect one ingot at a time clockwise from the active seat, beginning with Ada in this example.
learn_carcassonne_gold_result: Ada gets two and Bea one. When several features compete for gold, resolve the chosen completion order.
learn_carcassonne_magic_info: The mage adds one per distinct feature tile. The witch halves the modified score, rounded up. Follow legal relocation choices; remove a figure if it has no legal destination.
learn_carcassonne_magic_before: A completed three-tile city with one shield normally scores eight.
learn_carcassonne_magic_action: A mage adds three, then a witch halves eleven.
learn_carcassonne_magic_result: Round 5.5 up to six points. Apply modifications in that order, not by halving the base eight first.
learn_carcassonne_robber_info: A robber watches a rival’s physical score space, modulo 50. A qualifying departure can reward half the victim’s points, rounded up, without taking any away.
learn_carcassonne_robber_before: Ada’s robber watches Bea’s marker. Bea gains five points.
learn_carcassonne_robber_action: Bea moves and Ada accepts the robbery reward.
learn_carcassonne_robber_result: Ada receives three; Bea keeps all five. Robbery rewards do not create another robbery chain. A robber remaining at the end gives three points.
learn_carcassonne_crop_info: The active player chooses the allowed add/remove effect. Resolve clockwise starting to that player’s left, with the active player last. Follow the displayed figure/feature restrictions.
learn_carcassonne_crop_before: Ada is active with Bea and Leo following her.
learn_carcassonne_crop_action: Ada chooses removal for the shown feature type.
learn_carcassonne_crop_result: Bea resolves first, then Leo, then Ada. Removing a meeple also returns its attached builder or pig; an impossible required action is skipped.
learn_uno_wild_four_info: Here, Wild +4 is allowed even when you hold the active color. There are no +4 challenges.
learn_uno_wild_four_before: Ada holds a red 3 while red is active.
learn_uno_wild_four_action: She plays Wild +4 and chooses blue.
learn_uno_wild_four_result: Bea faces four penalty cards. This differs from standard UNO restrictions.
learn_uno_stack_two_info: A +2 can answer another +2 regardless of color. Penalties add together.
learn_uno_stack_two_before: Ada plays a red +2 against Bea.
learn_uno_stack_four_info: A Wild +4 can answer +2 or +4. A +2 cannot answer Wild +4.
learn_uno_stack_four_action: She plays Wild +4 and chooses a color.
learn_uno_stack_four_result: Leo faces six. Leo may add +4, but cannot use +2 against the top +4.
learn_uno_catch_window_info: The next accepted play or draw ends the catch opportunity. Rejected actions do not close it. A Wild opens the window after color choice.
learn_uno_catch_window_before: Ada’s undeclared last card is a Wild.
learn_uno_catch_window_action: Ada chooses blue; Bea then makes a legal play before anyone catches.
learn_uno_catch_window_result: Ada can no longer be caught for that earlier play. A failed illegal play would not have protected her.
learn_uno_short_stock_title: Too few cards and a draw
learn_uno_short_stock_info: Draw only what exists if a penalty exceeds the stock. With nothing to draw, a full rotation of consecutive empty-stock passes ends in a draw.
learn_uno_short_stock_before: Bea owes six cards, but only two can be drawn.
learn_uno_short_stock_action: Bea takes two and the penalty clears.
learn_uno_short_stock_result: If everyone later passes because the stock is empty, the game is a draw. A play or successful draw resets that pass count.
learn_catan_road_cost_info: A road costs one lumber and one brick. It must connect to your network without passing through an opponent’s building.
learn_catan_road_cost_before: Ada has one lumber and one brick and an open connected edge.
learn_catan_road_cost_action: Ada pays both resources to build a road.
learn_catan_road_cost_result: Her supply loses one road; both resources return to the bank.
learn_catan_settlement_cost_info: A settlement costs one lumber, brick, wool and grain. Outside setup it needs your road and an empty intersection with no neighboring building.
learn_catan_settlement_cost_before: Ada holds one of each required resource.
learn_catan_settlement_cost_action: She pays four resources at a legal intersection on her road.
learn_catan_settlement_cost_result: The settlement gives one point and produces one resource on matching rolls.
learn_catan_city_cost_info: A city replaces your own settlement and costs two grain and three ore. It is worth two points total, not three.
learn_catan_city_cost_before: Ada has a settlement, two grain and three ore.
learn_catan_city_cost_action: She pays five resources and replaces the settlement with a city.
learn_catan_city_cost_result: The settlement piece returns to supply. This place now scores two points and produces two resources.
learn_catan_development_cost_info: A development card costs one wool, one grain and one ore. Its identity stays private.
learn_catan_development_cost_before: Ada has wool, grain and ore.
learn_catan_development_cost_action: She pays all three and draws a development card.
learn_catan_development_cost_result: Only Ada sees which card she bought. Rivals see the card count.
learn_catan_road_building_info: Place up to two free roads using your remaining pieces and legal connections. If no road can be placed, finish the effect.
learn_catan_road_building_before: Ada has one spare road piece.
learn_catan_road_building_action: She plays Road Building and places that road for no resources.
learn_catan_road_building_result: She cannot invent a second piece; the effect ends after the one legal road.
learn_carcassonne_builder_figure_info: The builder belongs on a road/city with your meeple and has no majority strength. In 3.1 it returns when you extend that feature and grants an extra turn.
learn_carcassonne_builder_figure_before: Ada has a meeple and builder on an unfinished road.
learn_carcassonne_builder_figure_action: Ada extends the road with a new tile.
learn_carcassonne_builder_figure_result: The builder returns and Ada queues an extra turn. The meeple stays if the road is unfinished. Removing its attached meeple also returns the builder.
learn_carcassonne_pig_figure_info: A pig attaches to your farmer, adds no majority strength, and follows the 3.1 shield-city trigger. It is not a permanent field multiplier.
learn_carcassonne_pig_figure_before: Ada’s farmer and pig occupy a field.
learn_carcassonne_pig_figure_action: A shield-bearing city completes and the field neighbors two completed cities.
learn_carcassonne_pig_figure_result: The pig scores six without needing majority, returns, and offers Ada the choice to return its farmer. Removing the farmer otherwise returns its pig too.
learn_carcassonne_message_trigger_info: Choose one of your two markers for the turn’s point total. A positive active-player award landing on a multiple of five draws one message. Every message offers two points instead of its special action.
learn_carcassonne_message_trigger_before: Ada’s markers stand at 12 and 18; she scores three.
learn_carcassonne_message_trigger_action: She moves the marker at 12 to 15.
learn_carcassonne_message_trigger_result: Ada draws a message. Its special action is optional; she can take two points. Messages do not generate another message this turn.
learn_carcassonne_message_1_info: Provisionally score your lowest-value occupied city as if the game ended now, or take two points.
learn_carcassonne_message_1_before: Ada occupies cities worth four and seven at final scoring.
learn_carcassonne_message_1_result: Ada scores four. The city stays incomplete and its pieces stay. With no city, the special action scores zero.
learn_carcassonne_message_2_info: Provisionally score your lowest-value occupied road, or take two points. This does not complete the road.
learn_carcassonne_message_2_before: Ada occupies roads worth three and six.
learn_carcassonne_message_2_result: Ada scores three and keeps both road claims. No eligible road means zero for the special action.
learn_carcassonne_message_3_info: Provisionally score your lowest-value occupied monastery or garden, or take two points.
learn_carcassonne_message_3_before: Ada has a monastery worth five and a garden worth seven.
learn_carcassonne_message_3_result: She scores five without returning its figure. No eligible sanctuary means zero for that action.
learn_carcassonne_message_4_info: Take an extra turn after current decisions finish, or take two points. There must still be a tile to draw.
learn_carcassonne_message_4_before: Ada draws message 4 while tiles remain.
learn_carcassonne_message_4_result: After resolving current effects, Ada draws again. An empty deck proceeds to final scoring instead.
learn_carcassonne_message_5_info: Score two per shield in cities you occupy, or take two points.
learn_carcassonne_message_5_before: Ada occupies cities containing three shields total.
learn_carcassonne_message_5_result: Three shields give six points. The cities and figures remain in place.
learn_carcassonne_message_6_info: Score two per one of your figures in cities, or take two points. Count figures, not majority strength.
learn_carcassonne_message_6_before: Ada has two city figures, one of them large.
learn_carcassonne_message_6_result: Two figures score four. The large piece does not count twice for this message.
learn_carcassonne_message_7_info: Score two per one of your figures in fields, or take two points. No farmer returns from this message.
learn_carcassonne_message_7_before: Ada has three farmers on the landscape.
learn_carcassonne_message_7_result: Ada scores six and all three farmers remain.
learn_carcassonne_message_8_info: Choose one of your figures to return. Score its feature’s final value only if you are a majority leader; alternatively take two points.
learn_carcassonne_message_8_before: Ada leads a road worth four with one meeple.
learn_carcassonne_message_8_action: She chooses that meeple for message 8.
learn_carcassonne_message_8_result: Ada scores four and retrieves it, including any attached helper. Without majority she would retrieve it for zero points.
learn_carcassonne_gold_final_info: Each ingot is worth 1 point with 1–3 ingots, 2 with 4–6, 3 with 7–9, and 4 with 10 or more. Gold still on the map is not collected at game end.
learn_carcassonne_gold_final_before: Ada has five collected ingots. Two unclaimed ingots remain on the map.
learn_carcassonne_gold_final_action: Final scoring uses only her collected five.
learn_carcassonne_gold_final_result: Five falls in the 4–6 band: 5 × 2 = 10 points. The two map ingots add nothing.
learn_carcassonne_crop_add_info: The add effect permits a legal available figure on the indicated feature type where you already have a figure. This is an exception to ordinary unoccupied-feature deployment.
learn_carcassonne_crop_add_before: Ada has one meeple in a city and a spare normal meeple.
learn_carcassonne_crop_add_action: The city Crop Circle add effect reaches Ada after the other players.
learn_carcassonne_crop_add_result: Ada adds her spare meeple to that occupied city and now has strength two. Players with no legal target skip the required action.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_figure_info: The Abbot module supplies one strength-one abbot. It occupies a free monastery or garden, never a road, city or field. Completion returns it; you can also recall it instead of deploying.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_figure_before: Ada has her one abbot in supply and places a garden tile.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_figure_action: She deploys the abbot to the unoccupied garden.
learn_carcassonne_abbot_figure_result: The abbot remains until completion, final scoring or a voluntary recall. Recalling with four neighbors gives five points and returns the piece.
action_stale: The table changed. Review the current position and choose again.
action_match_changed: A new match has started. Choose an action on the current table.
action_timeout: The server did not respond. Reconnect to synchronize before trying again.
azul_description: Choose glazed tiles and build a brilliant mosaic.
library_azul_summary: A ceramic workshop for 2–4. Collect one color, complete your pattern lines, and connect tiles on your wall. Every tile counts—even the ones that fall.
azul_no_results: No matching lessons. Try another word.
azul_wall_conflict: This color is already on this wall row.
azul_choose_destination: {count} · {color}. Choose one line or the floor.
azul_marker_cost: Marker first: {cost} penalty; you start next round.
azul_changed: The table changed. Choose your tiles again.
azul_error: That move is unavailable. Choose again.
azul_disconnected: Connection lost · reconnecting. Your board is safe.
azul_tiebreak: Highest score wins. Ties compare completed rows, then share victory.
azul_practice: Local workshop · you control every seat
learn_azul_draft_info: For 2/3/4 players, set out 5/7/9 factories with four tiles each. On your turn take every tile of one color from a single factory or the center. Move a factory’s other colors to the center. Put your entire selection in one legal pattern line or directly on the floor. Turns go clockwise.
learn_azul_draft_before: A factory holds two blue, one red and one yellow.
learn_azul_draft_action: Choose all blue tiles from that factory.
learn_azul_draft_result: Two blue go to your line; red and yellow go to the center.
learn_azul_marker_info: The first center pick claims the first player marker and starts next round. Put the marker in the next floor slot before placing the selected tiles. Overflow fills remaining floor slots, then goes directly to discard. Floor penalties are −1, −1, −2, −2, −2, −3, −3.
learn_azul_marker_action: Take the marker and two tiles from the center.
learn_azul_marker_result: The marker fills slot seven; excess tiles go to discard.
learn_azul_pattern_info: Lines hold 1–5 tiles of one color. You cannot use a color already on that wall row. When the shared supply is empty, resolve completed lines from top to bottom: move one tile to its matching wall cell and discard the rest. Incomplete lines remain for the next round.
learn_azul_pattern_before: Line three holds two yellow tiles.
learn_azul_pattern_action: Add one yellow tile to complete it.
learn_azul_pattern_result: At round end, one goes to the wall; two are discarded.
learn_azul_cross_info: An isolated new tile scores 1. Otherwise count every contiguous tile along its horizontal connection and its vertical connection. Score each connected axis separately, including the new tile in both. A horizontal line of 4 and vertical line of 3 score 7. Gaps and diagonals do not count. Earlier wall placements in the same round count for later ones.
learn_azul_cross_before: A gap separates the two axes.
learn_azul_cross_action: Place the new tile at the crossing.
learn_azul_penalty_info: After all wall placements, subtract the occupied floor penalties. Your score never falls below zero. Discard floor tiles and return the marker to the center. Deal four tiles to each factory, emptying the existing bag before shuffling the discards back into it. If the total supply is insufficient, some factories stay partial or empty.
learn_azul_penalty_before: You have 2 points and four occupied floor slots.
learn_azul_penalty_result: You lose 2 actual points and finish at zero.
learn_azul_finish_info: The game ends after a round in which anyone completes a horizontal wall row. Everyone resolves their wall and floor, then adds 2 per complete row, 7 per complete column and 10 per complete color (five tiles). Highest score wins; ties compare completed rows, then share victory. Scores can exceed 100.
learn_azul_finish_before: One player completes a wall row.
learn_azul_finish_action: All players finish scoring this round.
learn_azul_finish_result: Add row +2, column +7 and color +10 bonuses.
learn_azul_conventions_info: This app uses the standard colored wall and 100 tiles (20 of each color). The first starter is chosen randomly. A marker claimed with seven full floor slots stays beside the board without extra penalty; its owner still starts next round. If no center color ever appears, there is no marker-only turn and the previous starter stays. Full pattern lines are not selectable; direct floor placement remains available. Round scoring is atomic and never waits for animation.
learn_azul_conventions_action: The marker never enters the bag or discard.
learn_azul_conventions_result: Public boards; future bag order stays hidden.
cn_description: A word table for friends: give clues, discuss together and uncover your team’s spies.
library_cn_summary: A shared table of 25 words hides spies, civilians and one assassin. Give a clue, discuss over voice and reveal your team’s agents before the other team.
library_cn_loop_1: Submit a word and a count.
library_cn_loop_2: Discuss, confirm a word, and find every agent.
cn_setup_hint: Each team needs one spymaster and at least one operative. Everyone agrees before the secret key is dealt.
cn_wait_ready: Choose every role, then everyone confirms. Changing roles clears all confirmations.
cn_win_agents: All of the winning team’s agents have been found.
cn_win_assassin: The other team revealed the assassin.
cn_error: That card or action is no longer available. Check the board and confirm a fresh choice.
cn_guide_setup_info: 4–12 friends form two teams, each with one spymaster and at least one operative. Teams can be uneven. All confirm their roles. Only spymasters receive the hidden key. The starting team has 9 agents, the other 8; there are 7 civilians and 1 assassin.
cn_guide_clues_info: The active spymaster submits a word and a count (0–9 or unlimited). Clues concern meaning, never letters, position or gestures. Avoid unrevealed words and their forms. Agree on exceptions together over voice. The app records clues; the group judges their legality.
cn_guide_clues_1: Submit a word and a count.
cn_guide_guess_info: Only active-team operatives can reveal after a clue. Discuss a word, select it, then confirm. Selection stays on your device. Competing confirmations require a fresh choice. An own agent permits another guess within your budget; a civilian or opponent agent hands the turn over.
cn_guide_budget_info: A numbered clue permits its count plus one guesses, including words from earlier clues. Make at least one guess, then continue or use End turn. Zero and unlimited remove the numerical limit. A civilian, opponent or exhausted budget automatically passes the turn to the other team.
cn_guide_budget_2: End the turn; the other spymaster gives a clue.
cn_guide_finish_info: Find every agent of a team and that team wins, even if an opponent reveals its last agent. The assassin immediately loses for the active team. Everyone receives the key at game end. The host can start a fresh board with new role selection. Team panels always show remaining agents.
cn_guide_connection_info: Reconnect in the same browser to recover your reserved team and role. An absent active spymaster blocks their clue; operatives must wait. After reservation expiry, a replacement inherits the role. Setup replacements clear readiness. Host promotion never grants the key. Reconnect clears pending selections. Clues, guesses and end-turn are never automatically retried.
cn_guide_connection_0: A seat disconnects; its role stays locked.
cn_guide_connection_1: Reconnect, or replace the seat after its reservation.
cn_guide_connection_2: Continue with the same team, role and board.
sgp_description: Build a delicious feast together: keep one dish, reveal, and pass. A complete Party! menu for 2–8.
sgp_summary: Choose your menu, collect delicious combinations and share the surprises. Three rounds. Every standard Party! dish.
sgp_loop_2: Pass left, collect sets and score
sgp_invalid: That choice is no longer legal. Choose again.
sgp_stale: The table changed. Review your current choices.
sgp_menu_invalid: Choose one roll, three different appetizers, two different specials and one dessert eligible for this table.
sgp_disconnected: Waiting for every guest to reconnect. Your choices are saved.
sgp_menu_intro: Choose the menu together. Every guest approves before the first deal.
sgp_select: Choose a dish from your hand
sgp_copy_preview: Your Special Order becomes this dish
sgp_copy_first: No dish to copy yet: this Special Order will be discarded.
sgp_prompt_spoon: Ask the table for a dish
sgp_prompt_supplier: Choose which matching dish to give
sgp_prompt_takeout: Box any dishes from earlier turns
sgp_prompt_attach: Put your copied Nigiri on Wasabi?
sgp_quick: Play three rounds. Secretly keep one card, optionally declare a previously played utensil, and reveal together. Resolve special choices, then pass the remaining hand left. Score combinations after each round; desserts stay for the final score. Equal final points use dessert count, then shared victory.
sgp_advanced: Numbered actions resolve from lowest to highest. Extra dishes take effect in this same turn; fresh utensils must wait. Miso collisions include every extra dish and copy. Spoon searches left automatically: only the supplier sees matching choices. Menu saves a private four-card offer until you choose. Special Order freezes a dish’s identity; it never creates another physical card.
sgp_conventions: C1 A copied utensil reverts to Special Order when returned to a hand. C2 Multiple utensils resolve by number, fixed seat order, then acquisition order. C3 Boxing either Nigiri or Wasabi breaks their link; an unboxed Wasabi becomes available again. C4 All-equal Temaki/Pudding counts apply both awards (only positive at two seats); zero Uramaki scores nothing. C5 Tea counts only this round’s desserts. C6 Boxed cards have no color, lose dessert status and score 2. C7 Equal points and desserts share victory. These edge conventions are deterministic app decisions, not verified publisher clarifications.
sgp_rule_nigiri: Egg 1 · salmon 2 · squid 3. An available Wasabi triples the next Nigiri.
sgp_rule_maki: Most icons: 6/3 at 2–5 guests, 6/4/2 at 6–8. Ties earn full points and keep the next distinct rank. Zero earns nothing.
sgp_rule_uramaki: Race to ten icons: 8, 5, then 2. Score and discard immediately. Tied crossings consume places. Most remaining earns only the next unclaimed award.
sgp_rule_temaki: Most +4; fewest −4. Full tied awards. No negative award at two guests.
sgp_rule_tempura: Every pair scores 5. Unpaired cards score 0.
sgp_rule_sashimi: Every set of three scores 10. Incomplete sets score 0.
sgp_rule_eel: One loses 3; two or more score 7 total.
sgp_rule_onigiri: Distinct shapes in each set score 1/4/9/16. You can build several disjoint sets.
sgp_rule_edamame: Each card scores one per opponent with any Edamame, up to 4 per card. Needs at least three guests.
sgp_rule_miso: Each surviving soup scores 3. If two or more appear in the same turn, discard all of that turn’s soups, even copies and extra dishes.
sgp_rule_chopsticks: Save for a later turn. Declare before reveal, then choose an extra card from your remaining hand. Return these Chopsticks to that hand.
sgp_rule_spoon: Save for later. After declaring, request any type or exact variation. The first guest to your left who has it supplies it and receives this Spoon. If nobody has it, discard the Spoon.
sgp_rule_menu: Draw four unused cards privately. Play one except another Menu; return and shuffle the rest. Discard this Menu. Only 2–6 guests.
sgp_rule_special_order: Copy one of your already played dishes this round, including shape, icons and priority. With no target it is discarded. Copied desserts stay for later rounds. Only 2–6 guests.
sgp_rule_wasabi: The next Nigiri must attach and scores triple. Each Wasabi holds one Nigiri. Shares a scoring color with all Nigiri.
sgp_rule_tea: Each Tea scores the size of your largest scoring-color group, including itself and this round’s desserts.
sgp_rule_soy: Each card scores 4 if you tie or lead for the most different scoring colors this round. Counts itself and only this round’s desserts.
sgp_rule_pudding: At the end of three rounds: most +6, fewest −6. All tied guests receive full points. No negative award at two guests.
sgp_rule_ice_cream: At game end, each set of four scores 12. Extra cards outside a complete set score nothing.
sgp_rule_fruit: At game end, score each fruit separately: 0/1/2/3/4/5+ icons earn −2/0/1/3/6/10. Double-fruit cards count both icons.
sgp_rule_tofu: One scores 2, two score 6, three or more score 0.
sgp_rule_takeout: Flip any of your dishes from earlier turns this round, independently. Each becomes a colorless non-dessert worth 2. Choosing none is legal. Discard this Box.
sgp_example_tile: Each illustrated tile is one card. Numbers show this example’s count or score.
sgp_example_draft_0: Choose one of these three cards privately: salmon Nigiri, Tempura or Tea.
sgp_example_draft_1: A keeps Nigiri and B keeps Tempura. Reveal both choices together only after everyone commits.
sgp_example_draft_2: Keep the revealed Nigiri on your plate. Pass the other two cards left, from A to B; every hand follows A → B → C → A.
sgp_example_nigiri_1: Add salmon Nigiri, worth 2: the two cards score 3.
sgp_example_nigiri_2: Add squid Nigiri, worth 3. Egg 1 + salmon 2 + squid 3 = 6 points.
sgp_example_maki_0: Three guests have 3, 2 and 1 Maki icons. Count the printed icons, not the cards.
sgp_example_maki_1: B adds a one-icon card. A and B now tie at 3 icons; C still has 1.
sgp_example_maki_2: In this three-player round, A and B each score the full 6 points. C takes the next distinct rank for 3 points.
sgp_example_temaki_0: Three guests have 2, 1 and 0 Temaki cards.
sgp_example_temaki_1: Compare every guest: A has the most and C has the fewest.
sgp_example_temaki_2: A gains 4, B scores 0 and C loses 4. The fewest-card penalty is omitted in a two-player game.
sgp_example_uramaki_0: A and B each have 7 Uramaki icons. No race place has been claimed.
sgp_example_uramaki_1: Both reveal 3 more icons together and reach 10 on the same turn.
sgp_example_uramaki_2: Both gain 8 and discard their Uramaki. The tie consumes first and second place; the next crossing scores 2.
sgp_example_tempura_0: One Tempura is an incomplete pair: 0 points.
sgp_example_tempura_1: Add a second Tempura to complete a pair worth 5.
sgp_example_tempura_2: A third Tempura starts another pair. The completed pair still scores 5; the spare scores 0.
sgp_example_sashimi_0: Two Sashimi are an incomplete trio: 0 points.
sgp_example_sashimi_1: The third Sashimi completes a trio worth 10.
sgp_example_sashimi_2: A fourth starts a new trio. Total: 10 for the complete trio and 0 for the spare.
sgp_example_dumpling_1: The fourth increases the group to 10 points.
sgp_example_dumpling_2: Five Dumplings score 15. Further Dumplings do not increase this total.
sgp_example_eel_1: A second Eel changes the whole group to +7.
sgp_example_eel_2: Three or more Eels still score 7 altogether, not 7 each.
sgp_example_tofu_2: A third spoils the group: all three score 0. More Tofu also score 0.
sgp_example_onigiri_0: A circle and triangle form a two-shape set: 2² = 4.
sgp_example_onigiri_1: Add square and rectangle. Four different shapes score 4² = 16.
sgp_example_onigiri_2: An extra circle starts a separate one-card set. The two outlined groups score 16 + 1 = 17.
sgp_example_edamame_0: A has two Edamame cards. B and C each have at least one.
sgp_example_edamame_1: Each of A’s cards earns 1 for B and 1 for C: 2 cards × 2 other guests = 4.
sgp_example_edamame_2: With five other Edamame collectors, the per-card cap is still 4. A’s two cards earn 8, not 10.
sgp_example_miso_0: A reveals the only Miso this turn. It can score 3 if no other Miso appears this turn.
sgp_example_miso_1: B plays another Miso during the same turn. Both soups are discarded for 0.
sgp_example_miso_2: C adds a bonus Miso later in that same turn. It is discarded too; the collision is remembered for the whole turn.
sgp_example_chopsticks_0: Keep Chopsticks on your plate from an earlier turn. Your current hand has Nigiri, Tempura and Tea.
sgp_example_chopsticks_1: Declare those Chopsticks with your primary Nigiri pick. After reveal, choose Tempura as the extra card.
sgp_example_chopsticks_2: Nigiri and Tempura stay on your plate. Return the Chopsticks to the hand beside Tea, then pass that hand left.
sgp_example_spoon_0: A has an old Spoon. B, the next guest left, has no Nigiri; C has salmon and egg Nigiri in hand.
sgp_example_spoon_1: A requests Nigiri. Skip B; C is the first matching supplier and privately chooses which Nigiri to give.
sgp_example_spoon_2: C supplies salmon Nigiri to A’s plate and receives the Spoon in hand. C keeps the egg Nigiri private.
sgp_example_menu_0: Playing Menu draws a private offer of four cards: Nigiri, Tempura, another Menu and Tea.
sgp_example_menu_1: Choose Nigiri. Another Menu cannot be chosen; the other three cards must return to the deck.
sgp_example_menu_2: Play the salmon Nigiri for 2 points, discard the played Menu, and shuffle the three unused offer cards into the deck.
sgp_example_special_order_0: You already have one Tempura, worth 0 alone. Choose it as your Special Order target.
sgp_example_special_order_1: Reveal Special Order as a second Tempura. The star identifies the copied card.
sgp_example_special_order_2: Original plus copy complete a pair for 5. The copy keeps its identity even if the source changes later.
sgp_example_takeout_0: An Eel from an earlier turn would score −3. You now play Takeout Box.
sgp_example_takeout_1: Choose that Eel and turn it face-down. It becomes a boxed card without a scoring color.
sgp_example_takeout_2: Discard Takeout Box. The boxed card scores 2 instead of −3, a five-point improvement.
sgp_example_wasabi_0: An unused Wasabi waits on your plate and scores 0 by itself.
sgp_example_wasabi_1: Play salmon Nigiri later. Attach it to that unused Wasabi.
sgp_example_wasabi_2: The linked pair scores 2 × 3 = 6. That Wasabi cannot multiply another Nigiri while occupied.
sgp_example_tea_0: Your largest scoring-color group is Wasabi plus two Nigiri: 3 yellow cards. Tempura has 2; Tea has 1.
sgp_example_tea_1: Count cards, not Nigiri points. The largest same-color group has 3.
sgp_example_tea_2: One Tea × 3 cards = 3 Tea points. These are in addition to the dishes’ own scores.
sgp_example_soy_0: A has four colors: Soy Sauce, Nigiri, Tempura and Tea. B has three.
sgp_example_soy_1: A has the most different colors, so each Soy Sauce qualifies for 4 points.
sgp_example_soy_2: Add a second Soy Sauce: still four colors, but two qualifying sauces score 2 × 4 = 8.
sgp_example_pudding_0: Save Puddings across all three rounds. Here A has two, B has one and C has none.
sgp_example_pudding_1: At the end of round three, compare total saved Puddings: 2 > 1 > 0.
sgp_example_pudding_2: In this three-player game, A gains 6 and C loses 6; B scores 0. Two-player games omit the penalty.
sgp_example_ice_cream_0: Three saved Green Tea Ice Cream cards are short of a quartet: 0 points.
sgp_example_ice_cream_1: Keep a fourth across the three rounds to complete a quartet worth 12 at game end.
sgp_example_ice_cream_2: A fifth starts another quartet. The five cards still score 12; eight would score 24.
sgp_example_fruit_0: One double-watermelon card gives fruit counts 2, 0, 0. Score 1 − 2 − 2 = −3 at game end.
sgp_example_fruit_2: Another double watermelon makes 4, 1, 1. Each fruit type scores separately: 6 + 0 + 0 = 6.
sgp_example_advanced_0: A declares Spoon number 4 while B reveals Menu number 7. Both effects wait in the saved queue.
sgp_example_advanced_1: Resolve Spoon 4 first, including its supplier choice. Menu 7 waits; hands have not passed.
sgp_example_advanced_2: Then resolve Menu 7. Pass the remaining hands only after all special choices finish.
sgp_example_conventions_0: C1: an original Chopsticks and its starred Special Order copy are saved on your plate. Activate the copy on a later turn.
sgp_example_conventions_1: C1: the extra Tempura stays on the plate; the returned physical card is Special Order again in the hand.
sgp_example_conventions_2: C3, a separate example: boxing only a linked Wasabi breaks its link. Box 2 + unmultiplied salmon Nigiri 2 = 4.
ls_description: Trade clues, hide your uncertainty, and uncover the intruders.
ls_summary: A secret society, two related passwords, and one very uncertain table. Speak a clue, debate, then commit a secret vote. First to five points wins.
ls_conversation: Use external voice or talk in person. With powers, everyone must also see one another by video or in person. The app records no audio.
ls_uncertain: Knowing a password does not tell you your faction. Never say your password or repeat someone else’s clue.
ls_no_word: You are the Journalist. You have no password. Listen and blend in.
ls_novice_hint: Give a normal clue, then stay silent during debate. You may vote.
ls_elder_hint: Give two words on your clue turn.
ls_sage_hint: While alive, choose one of the tied leaders for elimination.
ls_revenant_hint: When eliminated, you may eliminate another living player.
ls_adept_hint: No additional effect. Give one word.
ls_wait: Waiting for the required players. There are no automatic timeouts.
ls_guess_hint: One attempt: enter the Disciples’ password. Accents and ñ matter. Confirming ends your chance.
ls_reason_disciples: All intruders eliminated: every Disciple earns 1, including eliminated teammates.
ls_reason_survivors: Survivors: every Infiltrator earns 2 if one survives; a surviving Journalist earns 3. Both rewards can apply.
ls_reason_guess: Correct guess: only the Journalist earns 3.
ls_error: That action is no longer available. Check the current prompt and try again.
ls_scenario_journalist: Journalist: try a correct or incorrect guess
ls_guide_identity_info: Disciples share a password; Infiltrators share a related alternative. Neither knows their faction or teammates. The Journalist alone knows their role and receives no word. Keep your envelope private.
ls_guide_identity_2: Both may sound convincing. Neither word proves a faction.
ls_guide_setup_info: For 3/4/5/6/7/8/9 seats, deal respectively 2/3/3/4/4/5/5 Disciples, 1/1/1/1/2/2/3 Infiltrators and 0/0/1/1/1/1/1 Journalist. Choose English or Spanish words independently of interface language. Everyone readies; the first accepted volunteer starts.
ls_guide_setup_2: Three Disciples, one Infiltrator and one Journalist receive envelopes.
ls_guide_clues_info: Survivors speak one word in seat order, skipping eliminated seats. Never say your password or repeat a previous clue. Type your clue (up to 80 characters), then press Clue given. Mime confirms without text. Mime and Elder alter your clue; Novice stays silent only in debate. Use external conversation; players enforce spoken rules. The current host starts voting after discussion.
ls_guide_clues_0: Ada volunteers and gives her clue.
ls_guide_clues_1: Each survivor follows in seat order.
ls_guide_clues_2: Discuss, then the host starts voting.
ls_guide_voting_info: Living players must choose another living player: no self-vote or abstention. Select, then confirm an immutable ballot. Only commitment status is public until all have voted. Reveal all ballots together and count Dictator twice. Eliminate the highest total; ties require Sage or rock–paper–scissors.
ls_guide_voting_0: Ada selects Bea; nobody sees the target.
ls_guide_voting_1: Ada confirms and waits for the other ballots.
ls_guide_voting_2: All targets reveal together. A Dictator contributes two votes.
ls_guide_rps_info: A living Sage chooses only among the tied highest totals, including themselves. Without a living Sage, tied candidates confirm hidden rock, paper or scissors. One or three distinct symbols repeats the round. With two symbols, retain the losing-symbol group; repeat until one loser remains. Reveal each completed round together.
ls_guide_rps_1: Two choose rock; one chooses paper.
ls_guide_rps_2: The two rocks remain. They play again to find one loser.
ls_guide_journalist_info: An eliminated Journalist reveals their role and gets one confirmed guess of the Disciples’ password. Exact curated aliases are accepted after Unicode normalization, case folding and trimming/collapsing spaces. Accents and ñ remain significant. No fuzzy matching or host override. Success immediately ends the mission and awards only the Journalist 3 points; failure continues reactions.
ls_guide_journalist_0: The eliminated Journalist has heard clues about strings.
ls_guide_journalist_1: They confirm “violin” as their only guess.
ls_guide_journalist_2: If correct, only they gain 3. Otherwise play continues.
ls_guide_reactions_info: Reveal the eliminated role. Resolve a Journalist guess first, then an optional Revenant elimination, then scoring. A Revenant victim gets their own reactions. Withhold the solution until that eliminated player’s pending reactions finish. Resolve reactions even with two survivors. If play continues, start left of the original voting victim, skipping eliminated seats.
ls_guide_reactions_0: Bea is eliminated and has Revenant.
ls_guide_reactions_1: Without seeing the solution, Bea chooses Ada or declines.
ls_guide_reactions_2: If Ada is Journalist, Ada guesses before scoring.
ls_guide_scoring_info: After reactions, end when all intruders are eliminated or two or fewer players remain. If all intruders are gone, every Disciple gains 1, including eliminated teammates. Otherwise every Infiltrator gains 2 if any survives, and a surviving Journalist gains 3; both rewards can apply. Apply points together. At 5 or more, the highest total wins and tied leaders share victory. Otherwise every seat acknowledges the result before a fresh mission.
ls_guide_scoring_1: All Infiltrators gain 2; the Journalist gains 3.
ls_guide_scoring_2: Totals of 5 and 5 share victory. A lower total does not.
ls_guide_conventions_info: This is Spanish classic Little Secret (3–9), with the named seven-type classic power set, not US Secret Weapons or the French reissue. Powers default off; at 6–9 seats shuffle six distinct effects plus three Adepts and retain them throughout the match. The server chooses an unused original word pair and randomizes its orientation each mission. Words stay in the selected language. No forced timeouts: reconnect or use an available replacement seat. Rematch clears scores and returns to setup.
ls_guide_conventions_0: Choose powers only when everyone can see one another.
ls_guide_conventions_1: Factions change each mission; public powers stay.
ls_guide_conventions_2: Wait for missing actors. The host cannot invent a vote or guess.

domino_description: Venezuelan pairs dominoes on a patio table. Partners sit across; first team to 100 wins.
domino_choose_end: Tap where it goes — hold to slam
domino_tie: Tied count — no points this hand
learn_domino_deal_info: Use a double-six set of 28 tiles. Partners sit across from each other. Each player draws 7 tiles; nothing is left over.
learn_domino_lead_info: The first hand opens with the double six. After that, the lead passes to the next player, who may open with any tile.
learn_domino_match_info: On your turn place one tile touching an open end with the same number. Doubles lie across the line.
learn_domino_pass_info: You may pass only when none of your tiles fits either end. If you can play, you must.
learn_domino_out_info: The first player to play their last tile ends the hand. Their team scores every pip left in all hands.
learn_domino_block_info: If nobody can play, count each team's pips. The team with fewer pips scores everyone's pips. A tie scores nothing.
learn_domino_target_info: Hands continue until a team reaches 100 points. That team wins the match.
learn_domino_strike_info: Hold on the spot where the tile goes to slam it. A hard slam knocks the table out of line; anyone can tidy it. It never changes the rules.
library_domino_summary: Venezuelan dominoes for exactly four players in two fixed pairs. Everyone holds seven tiles from a double-six set. On your turn match one of the two open ends; pass only when nothing fits. Go out first and your team collects every pip left in the other hands. If the table locks, the pair with the lower count takes the points. Play hands until a team reaches 100. Rename the teams, slam a tile if you like, and tidy the table afterwards.
